cancer_indication: Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative (HR+/HER2–) breast cancer; approved in advanced/metastatic settings in combination with endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant) and as monotherapy after endocrine and chemotherapy failure; also approved as adjuvant therapy (with tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor) for high-risk, node-positive early breast cancer with Ki-67 ≥20%.
moa: Abemaciclib is a selective ATP-competitive inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6 that arrests cell proliferation by enforcing the G1 cell-cycle checkpoint. It prevents RB1 phosphorylation, maintaining RB1 in its active state bound to E2F, thereby suppressing E2F target gene transcription and blocking the G1→S transition. In HR+ breast cancer, estrogen signaling upregulates Cyclin D1 (CCND1), activating cyclin D–CDK4/6 complexes; abemaciclib disrupts this ER→Cyclin D→CDK4/6→RB1→E2F axis and synergizes with endocrine therapy.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Gene set representing E2F-regulated transcriptional programs that drive DNA replication and S-phase entry.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F output reflects the proliferative state governed by RB1; suppression of E2F targets is central to the cell-cycle control axis targeted by CDK4/6 inhibition in breast cancer.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.description: Gene set capturing early transcriptional responses to estrogen receptor signaling.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.interpretation: Estrogen receptor signaling in luminal breast cancer upregulates proliferative programs including Cyclin D1, linking ER activity to CDK4/6-dependent G1 progression.

REACTOME_CYCLIN_D_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_IN_G.description: Reactome pathway describing Cyclin D–CDK4/6-driven regulation of G1 progression through RB1 phosphorylation.
REACTOME_CYCLIN_D_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_IN_G.interpretation: This pathway captures the core G1 control module frequently engaged in ER-driven breast cancers, where cyclin D–CDK4/6 activity is a major determinant of proliferation.

REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_DURI.description: Reactome pathway describing Cyclin E–CDK2-mediated events controlling the G1/S transition.
REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_DURI.interpretation: Cyclin E–CDK2 provides an alternative mechanism to promote S-phase entry and can maintain G1/S progression independent of cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling.

REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.description: Reactome pathway describing dysregulated G1/S control in cancer caused by RB1 defects.
REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.interpretation: RB1 dysfunction removes a key tumor-suppressive checkpoint in breast cancer, leading to uncontrolled G1/S transition and altering the relevance of RB1-dependent cell-cycle control.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Gene set representing PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity involved in growth, survival, and proliferation signaling.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR is frequently activated in HR+ breast cancers and can sustain growth and survival programs that intersect with cell-cycle control and therapy response.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_FGFR1.description: Reactome pathway describing signaling downstream of FGFR1 through MAPK and PI3K-related cascades.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_FGFR1.interpretation: FGFR1 pathway activation promotes proliferative and survival signaling in breast cancer and can drive endocrine resistance and alternative growth signaling networks.

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_P16_CELL_CYCLE_G1.description: KEGG Medicus reference pathway describing CDKN2A (p16INK4A) regulation of CDK4/6 and the G1/S transition.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_P16_CELL_CYCLE_G1.interpretation: p16INK4A is a key regulator of the G1 checkpoint; its expression patterns reflect underlying RB1–CDK4/6 axis status and cell-cycle control states in breast cancer.

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_PDL_PD1_SHP_PI3K_.description: KEGG Medicus reference pathway describing PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint signaling via SHP phosphatases and PI3K-related signaling in immune contexts.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_PDL_PD1_SHP_PI3K_.interpretation: This pathway represents immune checkpoint regulation that can shape the tumor microenvironment and antitumor immune activity relevant to breast cancer treatment responses.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_HIPPO.description: Reactome pathway describing Hippo tumor suppressor signaling controlling YAP/TAZ-driven transcription and proliferation programs.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_HIPPO.interpretation: Hippo pathway integrity restrains proliferative signaling; disruption (e.g., via FAT1 loss) can increase proliferative drivers such as CDK6 and cyclins in breast cancer.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Gene set representing regulation of the G2/M checkpoint and mitotic progression programs.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: G2/M checkpoint and mitotic gene expression tracks overall proliferation programs in breast tumors and is coupled to broader cell-cycle activity states relevant to therapeutic control of growth.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: ER-positive (luminal) breast cancers often overexpress Cyclin D1 (CCND1) and rely on cyclin D–CDK4/6 complexes to phosphorylate RB1 and enable proliferation, indicating strong dependence on the CDK4/6-controlled G1 checkpoint.

High baseline CDK4 expression is described as a marker of dependence on cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling, consistent with the central role of CDK4 in driving RB1 phosphorylation and G1→S progression in luminal breast cancer.
Abemaciclib’s antiproliferative effect depends on an intact RB1 pathway; functional RB1 enables suppression of E2F transcription and G1 arrest.
In HR+ breast cancer, estrogen signaling (ESR1 activity) upregulates Cyclin D1 (CCND1), maintaining engagement of the cyclin D–CDK4/6–RB axis that underlies cell-cycle progression.
A strong ER-driven luminal program (including ER-related gene expression such as PGR) is described as characteristic of ER+ tumors where the ER→Cyclin D→CDK4/6 pathway is engaged.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Cyclin E1 (CCNE1) overexpression or amplification is described as enabling cyclin E–CDK2 bypass of CDK4/6 inhibition; absence or low activity of this bypass is associated with greater reliance on cyclin D–CDK4/6 control.

High p16INK4A (CDKN2A) is described as indicating an aberrant RB regulatory loop and poor response contexts; by contrast, low p16 is described alongside intact RB axis states that align with effective G1 checkpoint control.
Declining thymidine kinase 1 (TK1) activity reflects suppression of S-phase/DNA synthesis after treatment and is described as an on-treatment marker associated with longer progression-free survival.

Lack of PI3K pathway hyperactivation is described as a context in which tumors rely more on the cyclin D/CDK4 axis, whereas PI3K activation is described as a route that can undermine reliance on CDK4/6-mediated control.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Amplification or overexpression of CCNE1 is described in clinical cases of CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance and provides cyclin E–CDK2 activity that can maintain RB1 phosphorylation and S-phase entry despite CDK4/6 inhibition.

FGFR1 pathway activation (including FGFR1 amplification) is described as driving downstream MAPK and PI3K signaling, inducing cyclins and CDK6, and being enriched in tumors progressing on CDK4/6 inhibitors.
FGFR2 alterations are described as occurring in patients who progressed on CDK4/6 inhibitors, consistent with activation of FGFR signaling as an alternative growth route.

PIK3CA-associated PI3K/AKT/mTOR hyperactivation is described as a bypass survival/proliferation route implicated in resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition and addressed in combination strategies that co-target PI3K.

Upregulation of CDKN2A (p16INK4A) is described in non-responder contexts and linked to an aberrant RB regulatory loop; p16 overexpression is described as correlating with poor response in ER+ xenografts.

CDK6 upregulation is described as a resistance mechanism, including selection for CDK6 amplification/overexpression during prolonged CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure and as a downstream consequence of FAT1/Hippo pathway loss.
Resistant cells are described as showing increased expression of MYC and broader proliferative transcriptional programs that can support cell-cycle progression under therapeutic pressure.
KRAS mutations are described as emerging in some metastatic HR+ patients after CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and activating MAPK signaling that can promote cell-cycle progression.
HRAS amplification is described as emerging in some metastatic HR+ patients post-CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and driving MAPK signaling as a resistance route.

ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) is described as an efflux transporter substrate relevant to abemaciclib exposure; increased ABCB1 expression is described in preclinical resistance models as reducing intracellular drug concentration.
ABCG2 (BCRP) is described as an efflux transporter substrate relevant to abemaciclib exposure, contributing to reduced effective drug levels in preclinical contexts and sanctuary sites.
Anti-apoptotic signaling (including BCL2) is discussed as a factor that can allow survival during cytostatic arrest, with combination strategies being explored to convert arrest into cell death.

MCL1 is discussed as a survival factor where downregulation (e.g., via BH3 mimetics) can convert CDK4/6 inhibitor-induced arrest into tumor cell death, indicating that strong survival signaling can reduce depth of response.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss-of-function RB1 mutations or deletions are described as eliminating the G1 checkpoint that CDK4/6 inhibitors enforce, producing primary or acquired resistance because G1 arrest cannot be induced without RB1.

Loss of FAT1 is described as downregulating Hippo tumor suppressor signaling, unleashing YAP-driven programs that increase CDK6 and cyclin expression and correlate with shorter progression-free survival on CDK4/6 inhibitors.

Downregulation or loss of estrogen receptor signaling is described as reducing reliance on ER-driven cyclin D1 programs and diminishing benefit because the clinical benefit of CDK4/6 inhibitors is confined to ER-positive disease.

Loss of TP53 is discussed as potentially weakening stable checkpoint responses (e.g., p21 induction) and durable suppression under CDK4/6 inhibition, contributing to intrinsic resistance in some subtypes.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B): The strongest evidence for efficacy and mechanisms comes from luminal subtypes. Luminal A tumors (ER+/PR+, low Ki-67) are described as highly sensitive and reliant on Cyclin D1–CDK4/6 with intact RB1; luminal B tumors also benefit, but resistance mechanisms such as CCNE1 amplification and PIK3CA mutations are described as more frequently observed. RB1 alterations are described as rare at baseline but can emerge as acquired resistance after progression; tumors with high Cyclin D1 and low p16 are described as very responsive; PIK3CA-mutant luminal cancers respond but may have shorter duration and PI3Kα inhibition can be effective post-resistance.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-positive/ER+ (Triple-positive): Abemaciclib is described as showing efficacy in ER+/HER2+ metastatic breast cancer when combined with HER2-targeted therapy and endocrine therapy, supported by phase II data (monarcHER). These tumors are described as still relying on cyclin D–CDK4; resistance may involve upregulation of HER2/MAPK signaling (if HER2 therapy is suboptimal) or PI3K pathway activation, and toxicity monitoring is noted due to combination regimens.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC): Not standard for TNBC, but certain subsets may derive benefit. RB1 wild-type TNBC with high RB expression and low p16 is described as having some sensitivity, while ~20–30% TNBC with RB1 loss or inactivation is described as lacking efficacy. The LAR (Luminal Androgen Receptor) subtype is described as potentially more responsive and under investigation; abemaciclib is described as having CNS penetration and being trialed in brain metastases; TNBC often requires combination therapies (e.g., with immune checkpoint blockade) to be effective.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.gBRCA1/2-mutated or HRD+: Overlap mostly with TNBC or some luminal B cases; no direct contraindication described. HRD status is described as not clearly predicting CDK4/6 response and being orthogonal; some HRD+ tumors are basal-like (likely resistant due to RB1 loss), others luminal B (could respond). Data are described as limited regarding differential benefit by BRCA status.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Basal-like / Claudin-low: Described as typically RB1-deficient, p16-high, and highly proliferative (often TNBC) and generally poor candidates for CDK4/6 therapy, with expected rapid resistance via cyclin E upregulation or lack of effect due to absent RB.
